title: [FRONTEND-TASK-01-R] Reopen: Harden Challenge TypeScript Interfaces & useChallenges Composable
objective: Reopen and harden the core TypeScript domain models and the reactive useChallenges composable to support robust state management, query caching, attachment metadata, and optimistic updates.
specs:
- Framework: Nuxt 4 (Vue 3 Composition API, TypeScript 5.x)
- Target Files:
  * app/types/challenge.ts
  * app/composables/useChallenges.ts
- Interfaces to strictly enforce:
  * Challenge (id, title, description, business_process, status, difficulty_level, modality, min_semester, attachments)
  * ChallengeCreateInput, ChallengeUpdateInput, ChallengeFilterParams
  * AttachmentMetadata (id, file_name, file_size_bytes, mime_type, download_url)
- Composable API: fetchCatalog(), fetchChallengeById(), createChallenge(), publishChallenge(), closeChallenge(), uploadAttachment(), deleteAttachment()
acceptance_criteria:
- **Type Safety & Strict Validation:** All API request payloads and response envelopes must be strictly typed without any `any` or loose casts.
- **Optimistic Updates & Cache Invalidation:** Calling `publishChallenge` or `closeChallenge` must reactively update local component state and invalidate cached catalog queries without requiring a full page reload.
- **Error Normalization:** Composable must parse 400/403/404/409/422 responses from FastAPI/Nginx and return user-friendly localized error strings (e.g. extracting `detail` from JSON envelope).
- **Loading & Error Reactivity:** Every asynchronous action exposes reactive `pending: Ref<boolean>` and `error: Ref<Error | null>` states.
deliverables:
- [ ] Refactor app/types/challenge.ts with complete domain models and attachment types
- [ ] Harden app/composables/useChallenges.ts with error handling and reactive state
- [ ] Add Vitest unit tests in tests/composables/useChallenges.spec.ts
- [ ] Code passes pnpm lint and vue-tsc type checking
verification: cd frontend && pnpm test tests/composables/useChallenges.spec.ts

- Target Files:

  * app/composables/useChallenges.ts
- Interfaces to strictly enforce:
  * Challenge (id, title, description, business_process, status, difficulty_level, modality, min_semester, attachments)
  * ChallengeCreateInput, ChallengeUpdateInput, ChallengeFilterParams
  * AttachmentMetadata (id, file_name, file_size_bytes, mime_type, download_url)
- Composable API: fetchCatalog(), fetchChallengeById(), createChallenge(), publishChallenge(), closeChallenge(), uploadAttachment(), deleteAttachment()

---

title: [FRONTEND-TASK-06-R] Reopen: Redesign Voluntary Closure Modal with Strict Guard (ChallengeClosureModal.vue)
objective: Reopen and harden ChallengeClosureModal.vue with accessible dialog trapping, prominent warning banner, dynamic 15-character counter, and disabled confirm button.
specs:
- Component: app/components/challenges/ChallengeClosureModal.vue
- Props: isOpen (boolean), challengeId (UUID), challengeTitle (string)
- Business Rule: Closure reason mandatory with at least 15 characters (HU-08)
- Target Endpoint: POST /api/v1/challenges/{id}/close
acceptance_criteria:
- **Visual Warning Banner:** Prominent yellow/amber warning box inside the modal explaining: 'Voluntary closure will immediately remove this challenge from the public catalog and freeze active applications.'
- **Interactive Character Counter:** Textarea displays a live counter at the bottom-right corner: `X / 15 characters minimum`. Numbers turn red when X < 15 and green when X >= 15.
- **Strict Button Guard:** 'Confirm Voluntary Closure' button is disabled (opacity 50%, cursor not-allowed) as long as input length < 15 characters.
- **Submission Feedback:** On click, button displays a loading spinner. Upon successful close, modal dismisses, emits `@closed`, and triggers a success toast notification.
deliverables:
- [ ] Harden app/components/challenges/ChallengeClosureModal.vue with character counter
- [ ] Enforce strict 15-character disabling guard on confirm button
- [ ] Integrate warning banner and loading state
- [ ] Vitest unit test in tests/components/challenges/ChallengeClosureModal.spec.ts
verification: cd frontend && pnpm test tests/components/challenges/ChallengeClosureModal.spec.ts

title: [APPLICATION-TASK-09] Atomic Application Acceptance & Challenge Locking State Machine (RB-04, RB-05)
objective: Implement the atomic match transaction in Application service: accepting an application transitions status to ACCEPTED, locks the parent challenge to IN_PROGRESS (RB-04), and reveals reciprocal contacts (RB-05).
specs:
- Endpoint: POST /api/v1/applications/{id}/accept/
- Permissions: COMPANY role, Challenge Owner
- Business Rules:
  * RB-04: Atomic lock - challenge status switches to IN_PROGRESS; blocks any other applications.
  * RB-05: Reciprocal contact reveal - both parties receive unmasked contact information.
- Inter-service: PATCH /api/v1/challenges/{id} with status='IN_PROGRESS'
acceptance_criteria:
- **Atomic Database Transaction:** Status change of the accepted application and rejection/freezing of competing candidates executes within `transaction.atomic()`.
- **Inter-Service Challenge Locking (RB-04):** Calls Challenge service to set status='IN_PROGRESS'. If challenge service fails, transaction rolls back cleanly.
- **Contact Exchange (RB-05):** Returns student contact info (email, phone) in response and makes company contact info available to student.
- **Concurrency Guard:** Handles race conditions where two simultaneous accept requests hit the same challenge using `select_for_update()`.
deliverables:
- [ ] Implement ApplicationAcceptView with select_for_update() and transaction.atomic()
- [ ] Add Challenge service state transition sync client
- [ ] Pytest test cases covering atomic lock, rollback, and concurrency
verification: podman exec conecta-application uv run pytest -k 'test_accept_application'

### 1. Task Metadata & Traceability
- **Module / Microservice:** `infra`
- **Parent User Story:** HU-13 (Closes part of conecta-nexus/infra#8)
- **Assigned Developer:** @AnorakTeam
- **Sprint:** Sprint 3 (12 Nov – 02 Dec 2026)
- **Labels:** `task,sprint-3,infra`

---

### 2. Objective & Description
Stabilize and verify the complete 7-microservice local compose stack in compose.yaml, adding Mailpit SMTP mock container, volume persistency, and container healthchecks.

---

### 3. Technical Specifications & Constraints
- Target File: compose.yaml
- Services: postgres, auth, profile, challenge, application, notification, moderation, frontend, gateway, mailpit
- Mailpit Ports: 1025 (SMTP), 8025 (Web UI)
- Healthchecks: Configured on all microservice containers with 5s retries

---

### 4. Explicit Acceptance Criteria & Visual/Functional Specifications
- **Compose Validity:** `podman compose config` or `docker compose config` validates without syntax errors.
- **Mailpit Availability:** Mailpit container runs and web dashboard is reachable at `http://localhost:8025`.
- **Complete Stack Up:** All containers run concurrently in the local developer network without port collisions.

---

### 5. Deliverables & Checklist
- [ ] Add mailpit service definition to compose.yaml
- [ ] Verify container dependencies and healthchecks across all 10 containers
- [ ] Validate compose configuration

---

### 6. Verification Command
```bash
podman compose config || docker compose config
```
